name: High-water mark of a P&L
brief:
A fund's performance fee is charged only above its high-water mark, the best cumulative P&L so far. `pnl` holds the cumulative P&L at each day's close, in pounds, and it may be negative. Write `high_water(pnl)`, which returns a vector of the same length whose entry `i` is the largest of `pnl[0]` to `pnl[i]`.

For `{-3, -1, -2, 4, 2}` the marks are -3, then -1, -1 again, then 4 and 4, so the answer is `{-3, -1, -1, 4, 4}`.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 10^5$ days. An empty input gives an empty vector.
The size of the result is known before the loop, so reserve it.
hint: The first mark is the first day's P&L itself, not 0. Each later mark is the larger of the day's P&L and the mark before.

examples.note: A fund that only loses keeps its first day as the mark.

how: Submit runs 9 hidden tests. Each answer must be within a relative 1e-9 of the expected value.
notes: `reserve(pnl.size())` makes the room once, so the `push_back` calls never move the block.
Starting the mark at 0 would be wrong for a fund that never makes money.
`out.back()` is read only when `i > 0`, so the empty and one-day cases are safe.

planted.slip: Starts the mark at 0, which is wrong while the P&L is negative.
Reads pnl[0] before checking for an empty input.
The loop starts at day 1 and never pushes day 0, so the result is one short.
